editorial:
Don Winslow of the Navy is a Universal serial released January 6, 1942, directed by Ford Beebe and Ray Taylor. Don Terry plays Cmdr. Don Winslow, with John Litel, Claire Dodd and Walter Sande in support. It is a wartime story of saboteurs and a hidden submarine base under the Pacific island of Tangita. The Wikipedia article lists 12 chapters and 237 minutes, which makes it good raw material for serial supercuts, wartime-propaganda studies and Navy-themed compilations.

The rights trap is that this is not one copyright. The film is adapted from Frank V. Martinek's comic strip, so the strip's characters and story have their own copyright history, and the name is a likely franchise mark. We found no renewal entry for 'Winslow' in the 1969–1971 catalog volumes, but that search was partial and the Copyright Office catalog has not been searched. We therefore do not claim the print is free. Finish that check before relying on the print, and clear the strip separately.
faq: Is the 1942 Don Winslow of the Navy serial free to reuse?

Not confirmed. A partial text search of the 1969–1971 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes found no renewal, but the Copyright Office public catalog still has to be searched. The underlying comic strip is a separate question.
Does the Internet Archive upload settle its rights?
No. The Internet Archive items are uploads, and their metadata gives no license. Chapter 7 comes from PeriscopeFilm's archive. An upload shows availability, not copyright status.
